title: Experiment results aggregation jobs + materialized views for per-variant latency/cost/error metrics
creator: Chloe Martin
description:
Console results dashboard needs fast, consistent per-variant comparisons for an experiment over selectable time ranges (last 15m/1h/24h/7d/custom) with filters (region, route, project) and low query latency.

This ticket builds the aggregation layer on top of exposure events + request metrics to power the results query API (ENG-2841 / PR #18441) without scanning raw events.

Scope (v1):
- Aggregation jobs + materialized views (or incrementally maintained rollups) for:
  1) Exposure volume + exposure rate by variant
  2) Latency metrics by variant (p50/p95/p99, TTFT p50/p95, end-to-end)
  3) Error metrics by variant (5xx, 4xx, timeouts, canceled streams)
  4) Token/cost attribution by variant (input/output tokens, total tokens, estimated GPU cost if present)
- Query patterns needed by Console UI:
  - Timeseries (bucketed) + summary (overall) for selected window
  - Variant comparison table with deltas vs control
  - Guardrail-ready rollups (same metrics SRE alerts will key off of)

Non-goals (v1):
- Arbitrary dimensions beyond the allowlisted tag set (avoid cardinality explosion)
- Cross-experiment / global analytics (this is experiment-scoped)
- Quality/evals rollups (tracked separately under ENG-2846, but we should leave extension points)

Data sources (assumed):
- Exposure events emitted from gateway (ENG-2842): experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, project_id, org_id, region, timestamp, request_id (or stable join key), sampling_rate, schema_version.
- Request metrics stream (existing): request_id (or join key), latency_ms, ttft_ms, status_code, error_type, model_id, tokens_in/tokens_out, cost_usd (or token-metered cost), timestamp, region.

Key design choices / constraints:
- Keep experiment reporting stable under sampling: exposure events may be sampled; we must store sampling_rate to compute estimated exposures and avoid misleading charts.
- Avoid high-cardinality: only allowlisted dimensions in rollups: experiment_id, variant_id, route_id, region, (optionally) model_id if safe. Do NOT include user_id/api_key_id.
- Streaming: treat a streaming request as one request with TTFT + total latency; ensure we don’t double-count reconnects (assignment stickiness fix tracked in PR #18504).
- Late arrivals: expect telemetry lag up to ~5 minutes. Rollups should be correct with late events within a 1h window.

Proposed warehouse layout (names illustrative; adjust to current conventions):
- Raw/bronze:
  - ab_exposure_events_v1 (append-only)
  - request_metrics_vN (append-only)
- Silver (cleaned/joinable):
  - ab_request_facts_v1: 1 row per request with experiment_id/variant_id attached, plus request metrics/cost.
    - Join strategy: request_id preferred; fallback to (gateway_request_id, timestamp bucket) if needed (avoid unless unavoidable).
- Gold (serving / materialized):
  - ab_variant_rollup_1m_v1: per-minute buckets
  - ab_variant_rollup_5m_v1: per-5-minute buckets (UI default)
  - ab_variant_rollup_1h_v1: per-hour buckets (7d views)
  - ab_variant_summary_v1: summary over a requested window (can be computed from rollup tables)

Rollup metrics (minimum set):
- exposures_observed (count)
- exposures_estimated (sum(1/sampling_rate) when sampling_rate provided; else exposures_observed)
- requests (count of joined request_facts)
- success_requests (status_code < 400)
- error_requests (status_code >= 500 OR error_type != null)
- timeout_requests (error_type == timeout)
- rate_limited_requests (status_code == 429)
- latency_ms_p50/p95/p99 (approx quantiles)
- ttft_ms_p50/p95
- tokens_in_sum, tokens_out_sum, tokens_total_sum
- cost_usd_sum (if available), cost_usd_mean (derived)

Implementation notes:
- Quantiles: use warehouse-native approx percentile sketches (t-digest or equivalent) stored in rollup tables; mergeable across buckets.
- Backfill: support backfilling last 7 days for beta partners. Past that, rely on standard retention.
- Idempotency: aggregation job should be rerunnable for a partition (day/hour) without double counting.
- SLO for reporting freshness: data available within 10 minutes (p95) from request completion.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] Rollup tables exist for 5m and 1h buckets (1m optional if cheap), partitioned by day and clustered on experiment_id.
- [ ] Console results query API can fetch:
  - [ ] timeseries for a single experiment over 24h with 5m buckets in <2s p95
  - [ ] summary table for 2 variants over 24h in <2s p95
- [ ] Metrics match raw-event ground truth within expected bounds given sampling (validated with a reconciliation script).
- [ ] Cardinality reviewed and enforced (no unbounded tags). Includes automated checks/alerts on dimension explosion.
- [ ] Handles missing joins gracefully (exposure without request metrics): show exposures vs requests with a join_rate metric.
- [ ] Documentation: schema + query examples for ENG-2841/Console team.

Validation plan:
- Internal dogfood experiment on staging: run a 50/50 split, compare rollups vs direct raw queries for a 1h window.
- Replay-based test: feed a fixed set of exposure + request metrics events, ensure deterministic rollup output.
- Load test: simulate 50k req/min exposures sampled at 1:10 and confirm job cost/latency.

Open questions:
- Do we need route_id in every query, or is experiment_id sufficient for v1? (UI currently scoped to experiment; route filter is nice-to-have.)
- For cost attribution, which field is canonical: cost_usd from metering pipeline vs derived tokens*rate? Nadia prefers metering pipeline when present.

Requested UI contract (draft):
- /experiments/:id/results?start=&end=&bucket=5m returns per-variant arrays for latency_p50, latency_p95, ttft_p50, errors_rate, cost_per_1k_tokens.
- Also return join_rate so we can warn if exposure/request mismatch is high.

2026-02-13 — Mei Lin: Initial proposal: build ab_request_facts_v1 by attaching experiment_id/variant_id at ingest time (preferred) rather than warehouse join. If Caleb can add experiment_id/variant_id to request metrics stream in the gateway span, we can avoid request_id joins entirely. Looping in Caleb/Amara.

If we can’t, fallback join on request_id is OK but we must be careful about retries/stream reconnects creating multiple request_ids.

2026-02-14 — Logan Wright: Sampling semantics: exposure events will be sampled independently of request metrics. Store sampling_rate on exposure. For exposures_estimated, use sum(1/sampling_rate) but cap at a sane max to avoid weirdness if sampling_rate missing/0. Also note: sampling may be disabled for Dedicated beta partners (full fidelity).

2026-02-17 — Nadia Rahman: For cost, canonical is metering pipeline (cost_usd) where present. Tokens are still needed for UI. Suggest rollup stores:
- cost_usd_sum (nullable)
- tokens_total_sum
Then UI can compute $/1M tokens when cost_usd is null by using price book (but that’s later). For beta, if cost_usd missing, show token-based metrics only.

2026-02-19 — Mei Lin: Progress update:
- Created ab_request_facts_v1 draft schema (pending decision on attaching experiment_id at source vs join).
- Implemented rollup query for 5m buckets using approx percentile sketches (latency, ttft).
- Next: add error breakdowns and join_rate; then wire to a minimal results query prototype.

Blocker: need clarity from Vikram/Amara on whether request metrics will include experiment_id/variant_id tags post PR #18415 or if we’re expected to do warehouse joins.

2026-02-20 — Chloe Martin: Per Amara: gateway will emit exposure events; request metrics path is being updated to include experiment_id/variant_id tags when available, but rollout is staged. Suggest we build warehouse join path as fallback and prefer direct tags when present.

Also: UI will need per-region filter eventually; please include region in rollups but don’t add project_id unless we have to (cardinality).

2026-02-24 — Mei Lin: Implemented dual-path:
- If request metrics already include experiment_id/variant_id, they flow directly into ab_request_facts_v1.
- Else, nightly backfill job joins request_metrics to exposures on request_id for last 24h (best-effort) to improve coverage.

Added join_rate to rollups. Seeing ~92–95% join on staging; remaining are mostly canceled streams before metrics flush. Will document caveats so UI can show warning when join_rate < 90%.
